title: Focused cardiac ultrasound in the breathless or shocked patient
summary: Answer the questions that change emergency care: is the left ventricle weak, is there fluid around the heart, is the right heart under strain, and how full is the venous system? Learn the four views, EPSS, the descending aorta landmark, the IVC and the ultrasound JVP.
author: Dr Firas Abou-Auda, Consultant in Emergency Medicine and Course Director, Wavelength
conflicts: Dr Firas Abou-Auda is Course Director of Wavelength, which runs paid ultrasound courses.
audience: Emergency, acute and urgent care doctors, advanced clinical practitioners and physician associates who are starting focused cardiac ultrasound or supervising others.
outcomes: Place focused cardiac ultrasound within the assessment of the breathless or shocked patient, and state its limits
Obtain the parasternal long-axis, parasternal short-axis, apical four-chamber and subcostal views
Estimate left ventricular systolic function by eye and with E-point septal separation
Separate pericardial from pleural fluid and recognise the signs which support tamponade
Assess right ventricular size, the inferior vena cava and the ultrasound jugular venous pressure, then document and act safely
references: Via G, et al. International evidence-based recommendations for focused cardiac ultrasound. Journal of the American Society of Echocardiography. 2014;27:683.
